newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: CRICKET-SRI LANKA OPEN ASIA CUP WITH VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SRI LANKA OPEN ASIA CUP WITH VICTORY.

text.p: Pakistan's gamble to force Sri Lanka to bat first on a moist wicket failed on Monday when the world champions produced another spirited performance to win their Asia Cup match by 15 runs.
Sri Lanka, who made 239 all out in 49.5 overs, restricted Pakistan to 224 for 9 on a wicket which slowed down considerably in the second session.
Pakistani bowlers did well to curb Sri Lanka initially and restricted the world champions to 78 for 1 in their first 15 overs.
Sanath Jayasuriya, with several big scores in his bag, fell for only 33 before Mavan Atapattu steadied the innings, scoring 80 runs off 114 balls to win the Man-of-the-Match award.
At one stage the Sri Lankans looked like ending their innings with more than 250 runs when they were 160 for 2.
But a batting collapse, which included three run-outs in 17 balls, saw Sri Lanka lose their last eight wickets for only 79 runs off 94 balls.
Pakistan began their reply badly, losing their top three batsmen for 51 runs in 12 overs.
Despite a strong middle-order turnaround with the help of Salim Malik (57) and Inzamam-ul-Haq (48), the rest of the batsmen struggled on a slowing wicket.

Jayasuriya kept a nagging line to claim four Pakistan wickets for 49 runs in his 10 overs. Some superb outfield catches by Ruwan Kalpage helped Jayasuriya as four of Pakistan's wickets crumbled for 19 runs in just 15 balls.
Sri Lanka's win was assured once Imzamam-ul-Haq was run out when substitute fielder Upul Chandana's direct throw from backward square leg hit the stumps.
